newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi hospitals hit by civil service strike.
newsitem.headline: Malawi hospitals hit by civil service strike.

text.p: Services at eight state hospitals in Malawi were disrupted on Wednesday as a civil service strike over wages spread, union officials said.

At least three hospitals, the Queen Elizabeth Central hospital in the commercial capital Blantyre, the Lilongwe Central hospital in the administration capital, and one other in in southeast Zomba were operating on skeleton staff, an official from the Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) said.
The union called a strike of its members last Monday to push for a 100 percent salary increase which the government says it cannot afford.
CSTU vice president Mike Gondwe told Reuters those who could afford it were using private clinics.
Gondwe said five hospitals in northern Malawi were closed.
"No government hospital is operating at the moment. All of them are sealed," Gondwe said referring to hospitals in the north.
The strike has also spread to the Civil Aviation Department which has forced the closure since Monday of the country's second biggest airport, Chileka, in Blantyre, aviation officials said.
Flights have been diverted to the bigger airport at Lilongwe and passengers ferried 300 km (188 miles) by road to Blantyre.
